description: An associate general counsel must approve a proposed strategic agreement with an AI service provider and finalize its data-use, deletion, exclusivity, and customer-exit terms, with input from privacy counsel and the commercial partnerships lead.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to sign a strategic agreement with VertexMind, an AI service provider, next week.
shared_context.S2: The current draft permits VertexMind to use customer data for service improvement, allows deletion within 90 days after termination, grants VertexMind one year of exclusivity in the partnership's product category, and provides 90 days' notice for termination without cause.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the final agreement and its required commercial and data-protection terms.
shared_context.S4: The firm's contract-review routine requires the approving attorney to obtain a privacy review and a commercial-partnerships check-in before authorizing signature.

PF1.text: Marcus completed a privacy review of the proposed data flows yesterday and confirmed that the company's customer data may not be used to train or improve VertexMind models; the agreement must require deletion of that data within exactly 30 days after termination. He recorded the result in his working notes but has not yet added it to the contract comments.

PF2.text: Talia confirmed in a call with the largest prospective customer this week that the customer will participate only if the agreement has no VertexMind exclusivity and gives the customer a termination-without-cause right on exactly 30 days' notice. She has not entered the condition in the partnership tracker.

acceptance_conditions: VertexMind must not be permitted to use customer data to train or improve its models.
The agreement must require deletion of customer data exactly 30 days after termination.
VertexMind must not receive exclusivity in the product category.
The customer must have a termination-without-cause right on exactly 30 days' notice.
The agreement package must include a documented data-deletion commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The shared draft permits model-improvement use and 90-day deletion; PF1 changes those terms to a training prohibition, exactly 30-day deletion, and a data-deletion commitment.
The shared draft grants one year of exclusivity and 90 days' termination notice; PF2 changes the commercial package to no exclusivity and exactly 30 days' notice for the customer exit right.
